claim: Sulfate (SO42-) is the most abundant source of sulfur in the environment.
source: Sulfate (SO42-) is the most abundant source of sulfur in the environment and its utilization is contingent upon its entry into the cell (Kertesz, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kertesz, 2000.

claim: CysZ has been described as a SO42- permease.
source: CysZ has been described as a SO42- permease, but its sequence family is without known structural precedent.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: CysZ structures from three different bacterial species display a hitherto unknown fold.
source: CysZ structures from three different bacterial species display a hitherto unknown fold and have subunits organized with inverted transmembrane topology.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystallographic structure determination data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CysZ from Pseudomonas denitrificans assembles as a trimer of antiparallel dimers.
source: CysZ from Pseudomonas denitrificans assembles as a trimer of antiparallel dimers and the CysZ structures from two other species recapitulate dimers from this assembly.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data showing the hexameric assembly of PdCysZ.

claim: Sulfur is a vital component of several essential compounds, including the sulfur-containing amino acids cysteine and methionine.
source: It is a vital component of several essential compounds, including the sulfur-containing amino acids cysteine and methionine, in prosthetic groups such as the Fe-S clusters, as well as vitamins and micronutrients such as biotin (vitamin H), thiamine (vitamin B1) and lipoic acid, and in coenzymes A and M (Barton, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Barton, 2005, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: In prokaryotes, the entry of SO42- into the cell is mediated by four known families of dedicated transport systems.
source: In prokaryotes, the entry of SO42- into the cell is mediated by four known families of dedicated transport systems: the ABC sulfate transporter complexes SulT or CysTWA, the SulP family of putative SLC13 sodium:sulfate or proton:sulfate symporters or SLC26 solute:sulfate exchangers, the phosphate transporter-like CysP/PitA family, and the CysZ family classified as SO42- permeases (Aguilar-Barajas et al., 2011; Hryniewicz et al., 1990; Kertesz, 2001; Loughlin et al., 2002; Mansilla and de Mendoza, 2000; Sirko et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: CysZ family members are 28–30 kDa bacterial inner-membrane proteins found exclusively in prokaryotes.
source: CysZ family members are 28–30 kDa bacterial inner-membrane proteins found exclusively in prokaryotes with no apparent homology to any of the established channel or transporter folds, and are scarcely studied in the literature (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2014.

claim: An E. coli K-12 strain with a cysZ deletion showed a severe impairment in its ability to accumulate SO42-.
source: In two reports from thirty years ago, an E. coli K-12 strain with a cysZ deletion showed a severe impairment in its ability to accumulate SO42- and was not viable in sulfate-free media without an alternate sulfur source such as thiosulfate (S2O32-) (Britton et al., 1983; Parra et al., 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Britton et al., 1983 and Parra et al., 1983.

claim: E. coli CysZ functions as a high affinity, highly specific pH-dependent SO42- transporter.
source: More recently, a third report studying the functional properties of CysZ, concluded that the protein from E. coli functions as a high affinity, highly specific pH-dependent SO42- transporter, directly regulated by the toxic, assimilatory pathway intermediate, SO32- (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2014.

claim: The structure of IlCysZ was solved to 2.3 Å resolution in space group C2 by SAD.
source: Chronologically, the structure of IlCysZ was the first solved, to 2.3 Å resolution in space group C2 by SAD, initially based on a single selenate ion bound to the protein and subsequently also by selenomethione derivatization (SeMet) SAD, and multi-crystal native SAD (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystallographic data collection and refinement statistics presented in Table 1.

claim: The structure of PfCysZ was solved to 3.5 Å resolution with crystals belonging to space group C2.
source: The structure of PfCysZ was solved second, to 3.5 Å resolution, with crystals also belonging to space group C2.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystallographic data presented in Table 1.

claim: PdCysZ crystallized in multiple forms belonging to space groups P63, P4122 and P212121.
source: Third, we determined the structure of PdCysZ, which crystallized in multiple forms belonging to space groups P63, P4122 and P212121, revealing the same architecture and oligomeric assembly each time (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and Figure 1—figure supplement 2b.

claim: The CysZ protomer is an alpha-helical integral membrane protein with two long transmembrane helices and two pairs of shorter helices.
source: The CysZ protomer is an alpha-helical integral membrane protein with two long transmembrane (TM) helices (H2b and H3a) and two pairs of shorter helices (H4b-H5a and H7-H8) that insert only partially into the membrane (hemi-penetrating), forming a funnel or tripod-like shape within the membrane (Figure 2a,b).
evidence: This claim is supported by the structural data and Figure 2a,b.

claim: PdCysZ and E. coli CysZ sequences are 40.5% identical.
source: CysZ amino-acid sequences from different organisms are very similar; for example, those of PdCysZ and E. coli CysZ (EcCysZ) are 40.5% identical and those of EcCysZ and our three structures have 30.0% of their residues exactly in common (Figure 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: IlCysZ and PfCysZ crystallize as dimers.
source: Unlike PdCysZ, both IlCysZ and PfCysZ crystallize as dimers (Figure 3a,b), in agreement with their different behavior in detergent-containing solution.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and Figure 3a,b.

claim: Size-exclusion chromatography shows that PdCysZ elutes at 12.56 ml, IlCysZ at 13.42 ml, and PfCysZ at 13.95 ml.
source: Indeed, size-exclusion chromatography runs of the three species of CysZ in the same buffer and detergent conditions, show mono-disperse peaks eluting at 13.42 ml (IlCysZ), 13.95 ml (PfCysZ) and 12.56 ml (PdCysZ) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The dimer interfaces of IlCysZ and PfCysZ bury 780 Å2 and 1136 Å2 of surface area respectively.
source: The dimer interfaces of IlCysZ and PfCysZ bury 780 Å2 and 1136 Å2 of surface area respectively (Krissinel and Henrick, 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis data with a citation to the method used.

claim: The individual protomers of CysZ from all three species adopt the same topology and fold, and superpose well with an overall pairwise root mean squared deviation (r.m.s.d) of ~2.5 Å.
source: The individual protomers of CysZ from all three species adopt the same topology and fold, and superpose well with an overall pairwise root mean squared deviation (r.m.s.d) of ~2.5 Å (Figure 3c).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Disulfide-trapping experiments confirm the antiparallel assembly of CysZ protomers.
source: Disulfide-trapping experiments of the transverse dimer, performed by crosslinking a pair of mutants (L161C-A164C) on helix H5 of PfCysZ, as well as the corresponding pair in IlCysZ (V157C-Q163C) confirm the dimer interface observed in the structures of PfCysZ and IlCysZ, and, as a consequence, the antiparallel assembly of the two proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 2f,g,h).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental crosslinking data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2f,g,h.

claim: CysZ- cells showed significantly diminished SO42- uptake when compared to the WT strain.
source: CysZ- cells, after growth in minimal media and 12 hr of sulfate starvation, showed significantly diminished SO42- uptake when compared to the WT strain (Figure 4a), consistent with previous results (Parra et al., 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental uptake data shown in Figure 4a and a citation to previous work.

claim: All three species of CysZ displayed SO32- sensitivity in proteoliposome uptake assays.
source: All three species of CysZ displayed SO32- sensitivity and their activity was virtually indistinguishable from the SO42- accumulation observed in control liposomes lacking CysZ (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: The affinity for SO42- transport (Km) by CysZ is about 8 mM.
source: The further kinetic characterization of the three CysZ isoforms in proteoliposomes (Figure 4c) revealed that the affinity for SO42- transport (Km) by CysZ is about 8 mM (PdCysZ: 8.69 ± 0.35 mM; PfCysZ: 7.86 ± 0.72 mM; IlCysZ: 8.03 ± 0.68 mM)
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic measurements shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The maximum velocity of transport (Vmax) is about 90 μmol SO42- x mg CysZ−1 x min−1.
source: while the maximum velocity of transport (Vmax) is about 90 μmol SO42- x mg CysZ−1 x min−1 (PdCysZ: 100.4 ± 1.4; PfCysZ: 89.7 ± 2.8; IlCysZ: 87.9 ± 2.5; all values in μmol SO42- x mg CysZ−1 x min−1).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic measurements presented in the text.

claim: Catalytic turnover numbers (kcat) are 46.4 ± 0.7 s−1, 42.5 ± 1.3 s−1, and 41.9 ± 1.2 s−1 for PdCysZ, PfCysZ, and IlCysZ, respectively.
source: Taking into account the actual amount of CysZ incorporated into the proteoliposome preparations (determined with the Amidoblack protein assay, [Schaffner and Weissmann, 1973]) revealed catalytic turnover numbers (kcat) of 46.4 ± 0.7 s−1; 42.5 ± 1.3 s−1, and 41.9 ± 1.2 s−1 for PdCysZ, PfCysZ, and IlCysZ, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic calculations based on experimental data.

claim: Hyperpolarization of the proteoliposomes did not markedly increase CysZ-mediated SO42- flux into the proteoliposomes.
source: Potassium flux-generated membrane potentials of different polarity were imposed by adding the potassium ionophore valinomycin, revealing that hyperpolarization of the proteoliposomes (inside-negative membrane potentials) did not markedly increase CysZ-mediated SO42- flux into the proteoliposomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Depolarization caused about a 40% increase in the uptake activity of all three CysZ isoforms at a Kin/Kout distribution of 1:100.
source: However, depolarization (inside positive) caused about a 40 % increase in the uptake activity of all three CysZ isoforms at a Kin/Kout distribution of 1:100 (producing a theoretical Nernst membrane potential of +118 mV [Figure 4d]).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: The EC50 for sulfate binding is 3.51 ± 1.9 mM for PdCysZ, 2.24 ± 0.85 mM for PfCysZ, and 2.29 ± 1.04 mM for IlCysZ.
source: To determine the concentration of half-maximal sulfate binding (EC50), we isotopically diluted [35S]O42- with non-labeled SO42-, obtaining an EC50 of 3.51 ± 1.9 mM for PdCysZ, 2.24 ± 0.85 mM for PfCysZ, and 2.29 ± 1.04 mM for IlCysZ (Figure 4e).
evidence: This claim is supported by binding assay data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: CysZ binds SO32- with about 4-fold greater apparent affinity than SO42-.
source: Competing binding of [35S]O42- with increasing concentrations of SO32- revealed that CysZ binds SO32- with about 4-fold greater apparent affinity as reflected by a half-maximum inhibition constant (IC50) of 0.74 ± 0.23 mM for PdCysZ, 0.60 ± 0.21 mM for PfCysZ, and 0.56 ± 0.20 mM for IlCysZ (Figure 4f).
evidence: This claim is supported by competition binding data shown in Figure 4f.

claim: Single-channel conductance of IlCysZ is ~92 pS.
source: Recordings were made with varied membrane potentials applied in symmetrical Na2SO4 solutions on both sides of the bilayer, from which a single-channel conductance of ~92 pS was deduced.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological measurements described in the text.

claim: A bound SO42- ion was observed in the structure of IlCysZ.
source: A bound SO42- ion was observed in the structure of IlCysZ. This binding site was confirmed by purifying and crystallizing CysZ in the presence of the heavier SO42--analog selenate (SeO42-).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and Figure 5a.

claim: The bound SO42- is coordinated by two arginine residues (R27 and R28 in IlCysZ) and the backbone amides of residues G25 and L26.
source: The location of the bound SO42- is on the outer periphery of the CysZ protomer, close to the putative membrane interface where it is coordinated by two arginine residues (R27 and R28 in IlCysZ) and the backbone amides of residues G25 and L26.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: IlCysZ R27A/R28A, PfCysZ R25A, and PdCysZ R23A mutants all have severely impaired sulfate uptake capability.
source: In this vein, IlCysZ R27A/R28A, and the corresponding PfCysZ R25A and PdCysZ R23A mutants all have severely impaired sulfate uptake capability, as demonstrated in cells and proteoliposomes (Figures 5b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a)
evidence: This claim is supported by functional assay data shown in Figures 5b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: R129 mutants (R129E or Q) exhibited a severe loss of SO42- binding and uptake.
source: R129 mutants (R129E or Q) exhibited a severe loss of SO42- binding and uptake, and mutations made to Q176 and Y177 also showed loss in function, albeit to a lesser extent.
evidence: This claim is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: CysZ mediates sulfate flux into cells or proteoliposomes without coupling to ion gradients, partner proteins, or exogenous energy sources such as ATP.
source: Besides not resembling other transporter structures, CysZ mediates sulfate flux into cells or proteoliposomes without coupling to ion gradients, partner proteins, or exogenous energy sources such as ATP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing lack of dependence on ion gradients (Figure 4d and Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).

claim: CysZ features a novel protein fold that assembles as oligomers with an inverted transmembrane topology.
source: Combining the structural information from the three orthologs reveals that CysZ features a novel protein fold that assembles as oligomers with an inverted transmembrane topology.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data from all three CysZ structures and crosslinking experiments.

claim: The PdCysZ hexamer can be seen as a trimer of either IlCysZ or PfCysZ dimers.
source: In essence, the PdCysZ hexamer can be seen as a trimer of either IlCysZ or PfCysZ dimers (Figure 3f).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 3f.

claim: The refined structure of PdCysZ comprises an entire hexamer of near-perfect D3 symmetry.
source: The refined structure of PdCysZ comprises an entire hexamer of near-perfect D3 symmetry.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and Figure 1a.

claim: The hexamer has a triangular face of equal sides measuring approximately 75 Å, with the perpendicular span of about 65 Å.
source: The hexamer has a triangular face of equal sides measuring approximately 75 Å, with the perpendicular span of about 65 Å.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural measurements shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The interaction of the six protomers results in a total buried surface area of 5,700 Å2.
source: The interaction of the six protomers results in a total buried surface area (Krissinel and Henrick, 2007) of 5,700 Å2.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis with a citation to the method used.

claim: SO42- flux by PdCysZ, PfCysZ and IlCysZ is not thermodynamically coupled to the proton gradient or the Na+ gradient.
source: However, in contrast to what was observed for E. coli CysZ (Zhang et al., 2014), our data indicate that SO42- flux by PdCysZ, PfCysZ and IlCysZ is not thermodynamically coupled to the proton gradient (i.e., H+/SO42- symport) or the Na+ gradient (i.e., Na+/SO42- symport) but rather reflect the non-concentrative flux of SO42- characteristic of a passive, channel-like translocation mechanism.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Antiparallel insertion is fairly uncommon in membrane proteins.
source: Antiparallel insertion is fairly uncommon in membrane proteins; however, reported cases include the well-documented EmrE, a multi-drug resistant export protein that inserts into the membrane as an anti-parallel dimer, and the more recently discovered and studied family of double-barreled 'Fluc' fluoride channels (Amadi et al., 2010; Korkhov and Tate, 2009; Rapp et al., 2006; Stockbridge et al., 2015; Stockbridge et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on other antiparallel membrane proteins.

claim: A total of 63 different bacterial homologs of CysZ were cloned and screened for high-level expression and stability in detergents.
source: Following a structural genomics approach aimed at crystallization for structural analysis, we cloned and screened a total of 63 different bacterial homologs of CysZ for high-level expression and stability in detergents (Love et al., 2010; Mancia and Love, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by the methods description with citations to the approach used.

claim: The cysZ gene owes its name to its presence in the cysteine biosynthesis regulon.
source: The cysZ gene owes its name to its presence in the cysteine biosynthesis regulon.
evidence: This is a statement about the naming convention, supported by the context of the cysteine biosynthesis pathway.

claim: Once internalized, SO42- is first reduced to sulfite (SO32-), and then further to sulfide (S2-).
source: In certain fungi, and prokaryotes, once internalized, SO42- is first reduced to sulfite (SO32-), and then further to sulfide (S2-), a form that can be used by the cell (Kredich et al., 1979) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 showing the pathway.

claim: In E. coli, the culmination of the sulfate assimilatory pathway is the formation of cysteine by the addition of S2- to O-acetylserine by cysteine synthase.
source: In Escherichia coli and other gram-negative bacteria, the culmination of the aforementioned sulfate assimilatory (also known as reductive) pathway is the formation of cysteine by the addition of S2- to O-acetylserine by cysteine synthase, followed by the synthesis of methionine from homocysteine (Kredich, 1971) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The PfCysZ dimer is predicted to lie in the membrane at a 31° tilt to the perpendicular.
source: The resulting dumbbell-shaped PfCysZ dimer is predicted, by OPM/PPM (Orientation of Proteins in Membranes) (Lomize et al., 2012), to lie in the membrane at a 31° tilt to the perpendicular, in agreement with the position of its central hydrophobic belt, as revealed by surface-electrostatics calculations (Figure 3—figure supplement 2e,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational prediction using OPM/PPM and Figure 3—figure supplement 2e,f.

claim: The greatest variation between the protomers of each structure is seen in the orientation of helices H4b-H5a with respect to the TM helices H2 and H3.
source: The greatest variation between the protomers of each structure is seen in the orientation of helices H4b-H5a with respect to the TM helices H2 and H3 (Figure 3c), which seem to be the most conformationally flexible with respect to the rest of the molecule.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The structures that we have determined are evidently in a closed state.
source: In any case, the structures that we have determined are evidently in a closed state, implying that a conformational change would have to occur to allow passage of SO42-, likely modifying the surface electrostatics of the protein.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data based on the observed conformation.

claim: The binding of sulfate to the GLR motif could trigger a conformational change needed to displace L22, allowing for a wider opening for the sulfate ions to enter the pore.
source: Thus, the binding of sulfate to the GLR motif could trigger a conformational change needed to displace L22, allowing for a wider opening for the sulfate ions to enter the pore.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic hypothesis based on structural observations.

claim: Sulfite could hypothetically exert its inhibitory effect on CysZ function by binding to the sulfate-binding site.
source: Sulfite could hypothetically exert its inhibitory effect on CysZ function by binding to this site.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the observed inhibition and binding site location.

claim: The hexamer is maintained with the support and scaffolding of the lipid bilayer.
source: We presume that the hexamer is maintained with the support and scaffolding of the lipid bilayer.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observation that some structures crystallized as dimers.

claim: The antiparallel nature of CysZ could provide a means for internal as well as external regulation.
source: The antiparallel nature of CysZ could provide a means for internal as well as external regulation.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about the functional implications of the structure.

claim: Hydrophobic cavities and pores are seen commonly in ion channels.
source: Hydrophobic cavities and pores are seen commonly in ion channels, with examples ranging from the well documented hydrophobic inner pores of the various potassium channels (Doyle et al., 1998) to the SLAC1 (Chen et al., 2010) and bestrophin anion channels (Yang et al., 2014), and the MscS and MscL mechanosensitive channels (Anishkin et al., 2010; Bass et al., 2002; Birkner et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2010; Doyle et al., 1998)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to literature on ion channels.

claim: A pore through the three-fold axis of the hexamer could provide an alternative passageway for SO42- ions through this assembly.
source: A pore through the three-fold axis of the hexamer could provide an alternative passageway for SO42- ions through this assembly.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about an alternative transport pathway.

claim: CysZ SO42- flux activity may involve co-permeation of other ions with Na+ being the most likely.
source: Thus, we contemplate that CysZ SO42- flux activity may involve co-permeation of other ions with Na+ being the most likely for our experimental conditions.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the electrophysiological data.

claim: The putative pathway broadens after the narrow entrance, surrounded by a ring of conserved asparagine and glutamine residues, N33, N91, N98, Q176, and N220.
source: After the narrow entrance, the putative pathway broadens, surrounded by a ring of conserved asparagine and glutamine residues, N33, N91, N98, Q176, and N220 (Figure 7c-2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7c-2.

claim: The putative pathway widens leading into a large, primarily hydrophobic, internal cavity encapsulated by the TM helices of the PdCysZ hexamer.
source: Following this polar environment, the putative pathway widens even further leading into a large, primarily hydrophobic, internal cavity encapsulated by the TM helices of the PdCysZ hexamer, located in the plane of the lipid bilayer (Figure 7b and Figure 7—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7b and Figure 7—figure supplement 1c,d.

claim: The hydrophobic cavity is enclosed on both the top and bottom by pairs of helices H4-H5, three on each side from the six protomers.
source: The hydrophobic cavity is enclosed on both the top and bottom by pairs of helices H4-H5, three on each side from the six protomers, pointing in towards the three-fold axis, with each side of the cavity, at its mid-section, measuring ~50 Å, when viewed from above or outside the membrane (Figure 7—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1c,d.

claim: The entrance of the putative pore appears to be closed by the network of charge-interactions by conserved residues, R110, E106, N184, H185 and W235.
source: In the structure of PdCysZ, the entrance of the putative pore appears to be closed by the network of charge-interactions by conserved residues, R110, E106, N184, H185 and W235 (Figures 6a and 7c–1).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figures 6a and 7c-1.

claim: Pathway prediction algorithms performed on the CysZ protomer revealed a putative ion translocation pathway that begins at the entrance to the putative pore and ends in the large central cavity of the CysZ hexamer.
source: Pathway prediction algorithms (namely, PoreWalker [Pellegrini-Calace et al., 2009]) performed on the CysZ protomer revealed a putative ion translocation pathway that begins at the entrance to the putative pore and ends in the large central cavity of the CysZ hexamer that lies within the membrane (Figure 7a,b).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis using PoreWalker and Figure 7a,b.

claim: Mutations to N98 (N98A, N98D) led to impaired sulfate uptake.
source: Mutations to N98 (N98A, N98D) led to impaired sulfate uptake (Figure 5d).
evidence: This claim is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Charge reversal mutations made to E103 and E106 (to K or R) or the equivalent IlCysZ E107, E110 resulted in very poor expression and stability levels.
source: Charge reversal mutations made to E103 and E106 (to K or R) or the equivalent IlCysZ E107, E110 resulted in very poor expression and stability levels, suggesting that the disruption of the interaction network in this region may destroy the structural integrity of the protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations of mutant expression and stability.

claim: The GLR motif is well conserved among the CysZ family.
source: This SO42--binding site is in the loop between helices H1 and H2, with the motif GLR(R) being well conserved among the CysZ family.
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The internal concentration of SO42- at the peak uptake is only ~5 fold higher than the external concentration.
source: In fact, calculations of the SO42- accumulation in the PdCysZ-containing proteoliposomes at the peak of the uptake (at 15 s) shown in Figure 4b reveal that the internal concentration of SO42- is only ~5 fold higher than that of the externally added SO42-, whereas it is ~3 fold elevated at the plateau (120 s), revealing non-concentrative SO42- flux by CysZ that is representative for a channel-like mode of action (see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: This claim is supported by calculations based on experimental data from Figure 4b.

claim: MhsT-mediated Na+-coupled L-tryptophan transport yields an ~150 fold internal concentration excess of the amino acid.
source: Note that applying the same calculation to the MhsT-mediated Na+-coupled L-tryptophan transport in the identical preparation of MhsT-containing proteoliposomes (Malinauskaite et al., 2014) yields an ~150 fold internal concentration excess of the amino acid.
evidence: This claim is supported by calculations based on data from a cited study (Malinauskaite et al., 2014).

claim: WT cells showed fast accumulation of 320 μM [35S]O42- that was linear over a period of 3 min.
source: WT cells showed fast accumulation of 320 μM [35S]O42- that was linear over a period of 3 min, whereas uptake of [35S]O42- by the CysZ- strain started to plateau after about 1 min.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The three orthologs (PdCysZ, PfCysZ and IlCysZ) all mediated the accumulation of 500 μM SO42- into proteoliposomes in a manner virtually indistinguishable from one another.
source: Consistent with the cell uptake studies, the three orthologs (PdCysZ, PfCysZ and IlCysZ) all mediated the accumulation of 500 μM SO42- into proteoliposomes in a manner virtually indistinguishable from one another.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Uptake was time-dependent and occurred rapidly with a peak at about 15 s.
source: Uptake was time-dependent and occurred rapidly with a peak at about 15 s (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: ~3 mM SO32- resulted in half-maximum inhibition (IC50) of SO42- uptake.
source: Measuring uptake of 1 mM [35S]O42- in the presence of increasing concentrations of SO32- showed that ~3 mM SO32- resulted in half-maximum inhibition (IC50) of SO42- uptake under those experimental conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: MST-based binding of SO32- revealed apparent affinities for SO32- binding by PdCysZ and IlCysZ of 3.73 ± 0.76 mM and 8.68 ± 1.88 mM, respectively.
source: Whereas the SPA-based binding competition of [35S]O42- binding by SO32- represents an indirect assay, MST-based binding of SO32- revealed apparent affinities for SO32- binding by PdCysZ and IlCysZ of 3.73 ± 0.76 mM and 8.68 ± 1.88 mM, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by MST binding data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1d.

claim: Measurements made with PdCysZ gave a similar single-channel conductance level to IlCysZ.
source: Measurements made with PdCysZ gave a similar single-channel conductance level.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological measurements described in the text.

claim: Reconstituted CysZ exhibits channel-like properties.
source: Thus, consistent with our [35S]O42--based flux assays, these electrophysiological measurements showed that reconstituted CysZ exhibits channel-like properties.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiological data.

claim: The protein has an extra-membranous hydrophilic 'head', comprising an iris-like arrangement of the two short helices, H1 and H6, and kinked helices H3b, H4a, and H5b.
source: The protein has an extra-membranous hydrophilic 'head', comprising an iris-like arrangement of the two short helices, H1 and H6, and kinked helices H3b, H4a, and H5b.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2a,b.

claim: The amino and carboxyl termini are located in the hydrophilic head region.
source: The amino and carboxyl termini are also located in this region (Figure 2a,b).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2a,b.

claim: Helices H4b and H5a lie partly inserted in the membrane, with the turn between the two pointing in towards the three-fold axis at the center of the hexamer.
source: Helices H4b and H5a lie partly inserted in the membrane, with the turn between the two pointing in towards the three-fold axis at the center of the hexamer.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data.

claim: EcCysZ and the three structures have 30.0% of their residues exactly in common.
source: CysZ amino-acid sequences from different organisms are very similar; for example, those of PdCysZ and E. coli CysZ (EcCysZ) are 40.5% identical and those of EcCysZ and our three structures have 30.0% of their residues exactly in common (Figure 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Helix boundaries are essentially the same in the structures of PdCysZ, IlCysZ and PfCysZ.
source: Helix boundaries are also essentially the same in the structures of PdCysZ, IlCysZ and PfCysZ (Figure 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Antiparallel pairs of protomers arrange together as a trimer of dimers.
source: Antiparallel pairs of protomers arrange together as a trimer of dimers (Figure 1a), with the three-fold axis oriented perpendicular to the plane of the putative membrane and three two-fold axes between dimers of the hexamer.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Both the periplasmic and cytoplasmic faces of the hexamer are essentially identical by symmetry, resulting in a dual-topology assembly for PdCysZ.
source: Both the periplasmic and cytoplasmic faces of the hexamer are essentially identical by symmetry, resulting in a dual-topology assembly for PdCysZ.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis of the PdCysZ hexamer.

claim: A surface electrostatic representation reveals a hydrophobic belt along the mid-section of the hexamer when viewed from its side.
source: A surface electrostatic representation reveals a hydrophobic belt along the mid-section of the hexamer when viewed from its side, outlining the orientation of CysZ in the lipid bilayer (Czodrowski et al., 2006; Dolinsky et al., 2007; Dolinsky et al., 2004) (Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by surface electrostatics calculations shown in Figure 1b.

claim: A surface representation of the sequence conservation highlights the regions of invariance in the sequence.
source: A surface representation of the sequence conservation, calculated by analysis of multiple sequence alignments (MSA) (Ashkenazy et al., 2016; Glaser et al., 2003) highlights the regions of invariance in the sequence and in turn, the areas on the molecule that are most likely to have structural and functional importance (Figure 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by conservation analysis shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The protomers of the IlCysZ dimer are arranged in a head-to-tail antiparallel association.
source: The protomers of the IlCysZ dimer are arranged in a head-to-tail antiparallel association, with helices H4b-H5a protruding at an angle that is nearly parallel to the putative plane of the membrane (Figure 3a and -figure supplement 2a,b).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3a and Figure 3—figure supplement 2a,b.

claim: The PfCysZ dimer is arranged in an antiparallel orientation but with a different dimer interface.
source: The PfCysZ dimer is also arranged in an antiparallel orientation but with a different dimer interface (Figure 3b).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: In the PfCysZ structure, helices H4b-H5a together form a narrower angle with helices H2 and H3, and tuck-in closer to the rest of the molecule.
source: In the PfCysZ structure, helices H4b-H5a together form a narrower angle with helices H2 and H3, and tuck-in closer to the rest of the molecule (Figure 3b).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The IlCysZ dimer resembles the vertically arranged pair of protomers in the PdCysZ hexamer at each of the vertices of the triangular structure.
source: Indeed, the IlCysZ dimer (Figure 3a) resembles the vertically arranged pair of protomers in the PdCysZ hexamer (Figure 3d) at each of the vertices of the triangular structure.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figures 3a and 3d.

claim: The PfCysZ dimer resembles the transverse pair of protomers lying at a tilt along the side of the PdCysZ hexamer.
source: On the other hand, the PfCysZ dimer (Figure 3b) resembles the transverse pair of protomers lying at a tilt, just as was predicted by OPM (Lomize et al., 2012), along the side of the PdCysZ hexamer when viewed from inside the plane of the membrane (Figure 3e).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figures 3b and 3e.

claim: The low level of sulfate accumulation by the CysZ- strain could be attributed to other endogenous sulfate transport systems present in the bacteria.
source: This low level of sulfate accumulation by the CysZ- strain could be attributed to the other endogenous sulfate transport systems present in the bacteria (for example ABC transporter and SulP).
evidence: This is an inference based on known sulfate transport systems in bacteria.

claim: The view into a protomer surface along the direct pathway between transverse dimer apices displays the pattern of exceptionally high conservation associated with the entrance to a putative pore for sulfate translocation.
source: The view into a protomer surface along the direct pathway between transverse dimer apices (e.g. green to orange in Figure 3e) displays the pattern of exceptionally high conservation associated with the entrance to a putative pore for sulfate translocation (Figure 6a,b).
evidence: This claim is supported by conservation analysis shown in Figure 6a,b.

claim: This putative pore-entrance lies approximately 17–20 Å (linear distance) away from the observed sulfate binding site.
source: Intriguingly, this putative pore-entrance lies approximately 17–20 Å (linear distance) away from the observed sulfate binding site.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural measurements.

claim: The electrostatic potential surface of PdCysZ shows striking and puzzling electronegativity at the conserved pore entrance.
source: The electrostatic potential surface of PdCysZ (Figure 6c) shows striking and puzzling electronegativity at the conserved pore entrance (Figure 6d compared with Figure 6b).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrostatic calculations shown in Figure 6c,d.

claim: We observe the same helix dispositions, pore shape and charge interactions in all three structures.
source: Moreover, we observe the same helix dispositions, pore shape and charge interactions in all three structures, evident when the protomers are superimposed (Figure 3c, top view).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The putative entrance or 'pore' lies in the midst of a tight network of interacting residues.
source: This putative entrance or 'pore' lies in the midst of a tight network of interacting residues, which is seen detailed in the inset of Figure 5c in the very same view as for Figure 6a.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 5c and Figure 6a.

claim: These interactions close the incipient pore from ion conduction in this conformation.
source: These interactions close the incipient pore from ion conduction in this conformation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: The central core of the hydrophilic head consists of the ends of helices H3 and H5 and the start of helix H4.
source: The central core of this hydrophilic head consists of the ends of helices H3 and H5 and the start of helix H4, with their residues forming an intricate network of hydrogen bonds and salt bridges that hold this helical bundle together (Figure 5c).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Two highly conserved motifs in the hydrophilic head region are ExVE and QYxDYPxDNHK.
source: Two highly conserved motifs in this region, ExVE and QYxDYPxDNHK (Figure 2c), likely play critical roles in this network of interactions.
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence conservation data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The two aspartates E103 and E106 (PdCysZ) in the first motif interact with R129, N184 and R110, H185, respectively.
source: The two aspartates E103 and E106 (PdCysZ) in the first motif interact with R129, N184 and R110, H185, respectively (Figure 5c).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The conserved R129 and R133 on helix H4b interact with D183 and N184 in the DNHK sequence stretch of helix H5b.
source: The conserved R129 and R133 on helix H4b in turn also interact with D183 and N184 in the DNHK sequence stretch of helix H5b in the second motif.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: A conserved tyrosine (Y177) lies below the membrane interface towards the core of the molecule, along helix H5.
source: In the second motif, a conserved tyrosine (Y177) lies below the membrane interface towards the core of the molecule, along helix H5.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data.

claim: Mutations made to Q176 and Y177 showed loss in function, albeit to a lesser extent than R129 mutants.
source: R129 mutants (R129E or Q) exhibited a severe loss of SO42- binding and uptake, and mutations made to Q176 and Y177 also showed loss in function, albeit to a lesser extent.
evidence: This claim is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: There is a conserved central core which is likely to have a structural role.
source: There is a conserved central core (Figure 6a), which is likely to have a structural role.
evidence: This is an inference based on the high conservation of the core region.

claim: Sulfate ions that might enter through the three separate pores would converge into a central hydrophobic cavity.
source: Following this hypothetical route, sulfate ions that might enter through the three separate pores, one per CysZ dimer pair, would converge into a central hydrophobic cavity (Figure 7b and Figure 7—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis based on the structural features.

claim: Once sulfate ions enter the central cavity, they are likely to exit it rather rapidly through one of the three available exit pores on the cytoplasmic side.
source: Once sulfate ions enter this central cavity, due to the unfavorable environment, these are likely to exit it rather rapidly through one of the three available exit pores on the cytoplasmic side of the hexamer.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis based on the hydrophobic nature of the cavity.

claim: The surface electrostatics of CysZ draw attention to the negative potential of the conserved core of each protomer.
source: The surface electrostatics of CysZ (Figures 1b and 6c,d) draw attention to the negative potential of the conserved core of each protomer, which is then surrounded by a more neutral annulus.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrostatic calculations shown in Figures 1b and 6c,d.

claim: While the negative potential seems contradictory to admission of SO42- ions at the extracellular side, it could be advantageous for expulsion into the cytoplasm on the opposite side.
source: While this feature seems contradictory to admission of SO42- ions at the extracellular side, it could be advantageous for expulsion into the cytoplasm on the opposite side.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the electrostatic properties.

claim: A conformational change would have to occur to allow passage of SO42-.
source: In any case, the structures that we have determined are evidently in a closed state, implying that a conformational change would have to occur to allow passage of SO42-, likely modifying the surface electrostatics of the protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the closed state of the structure.

claim: There is an overall electropositive region in the center of the hexameric molecule when viewed from the top.
source: There is an overall electropositive region in the center of the hexameric molecule, when viewed from the top (Figures 1b and 6c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrostatic calculations shown in Figures 1b and 6c,d.

claim: This central region is lined by conserved residues along helices H4b-H5a, namely, R129, R133 and K137.
source: This central region is lined by conserved residues along helices H4b-H5a, namely, R129, R133 and K137.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis.

claim: The hydrophobic tips of helices H4b-H5a of the three protomers on each side of the membrane converge in the center of the hexamer.
source: The hydrophobic tips of helices H4b-H5a of the three protomers on each side of the membrane then converge in the center of the hexamer.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data.

claim: CysZ is a hexamer in nature, as observed in PdCysZ.
source: Thus, we hypothesize that CysZ is a hexamer in nature, as observed in PdCysZ, consistent with the fact that all CysZs studied here exhibit essentially the same functional properties.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on structural and functional data.

claim: In the case of IlCysZ and PfCysZ, the hexameric assembly may have come apart into dimeric components during detergent extraction and purification.
source: In the case of IlCysZ and PfCysZ, this assembly may have come apart into the subsequently crystallized dimeric components during the process of detergent extraction from the membrane and purification.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed dimeric structures.

claim: This could be explained by the unusually labile, and conformationally-flexible, nature of the H4b-H5a helical hairpin of CysZ.
source: This could be explained by the unusually labile, and conformationally-flexible, nature of the H4b-H5a helical hairpin of CysZ, with only one pair of stabilizing TM helices per protomer (H2-H3).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation based on structural observations.

claim: IlCysZ can adopt both of the dimer assemblies observed in the PdCysZ hexamer.
source: Furthermore, IlCysZ can be crosslinked in membranes to the alternative PfCysZ dimer by engineering of disulfide cysteine mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), which suggests that IlCysZ can adopt both of the dimer assemblies observed in the PdCysZ hexamer.
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.
